title: Financial ABM: an auditable multi-agent artificial market for ESG disclosure and greenwashing policy experiments
description: Code, configurations, pre-registrations and evidence for the working paper Greenwashing Moves to Where Enforcement Is Weakest: Pre-Registered Experiments in an Artificial Market (Ellis Lin, 2026). An agent-based artificial financial market in which profit-maximising and impact investors evolve by imitation, firms choose between real improvement, greenwashing and maintenance, and a regulator sets transparency, audits and fines. The archive contains fourteen pre-registered studies spanning stage F (59 scenarios x 30 paired seeds) and its exploratory supplements, joint robustness (24 scenarios x 30 seeds), targeted audits (15 scenarios x 30 seeds), assurance providers (18 scenarios x 30 seeds), learning firms (10 independent trainings per scenario), empirical persistence, financing-channel and investor-response checks (stages H-J), and seven MAS mechanism-design upgrade studies (contract §§29-32, 2,250 confirmatory runs covering Bayesian dynamic RMAB-Stackelberg auditing, G-band communication menus, zero-leakage empirical-belief learning, partial-observability assurance hysteresis/floor Pareto frontiers, Q-dynamics reversal and non-ESG AI-washing generalisation), together with the 11-figure reproduction package. Manuscript sources are maintained separately; vendor data without a redistribution licence are not included, while collection scripts and hash manifests are. Results are conditional on the model.
